### Make a Free Survey in Minutes

Creating a survey has never been this simple. Add your questions in the survey creator above,
customize the design to match your style, and start collecting responses within minutes, no survey
or response limits. Your survey is instantly optimized for mobile, tablet, or desktop and can be
shared effortlessly through a single click. Looking for inspiration? Our AI-powered survey
generator, trained on thousands of expertly crafted surveys, can create a tailored survey for your
exact needs in seconds. It's fast, intuitive, and ready to help you get results.

[Effortless Survey Creation]
[Wide Question Variety]

### Ask Any Question, Your Way

With 40+ question types, Super Survey empowers you to create any survey imaginable. Whether you need
multiple choice, open-ended text, rating scales, or advanced logic-based questions, our platform has
you covered. From simple feedback forms to detailed market research surveys - or even interactive
quizzes - Super Survey offers unmatched flexibility. We're the only platform that combines robust
survey capabilities with quiz creation, enabling you to gather data, test knowledge, or engage
audiences all in one place. With Super Survey, you can ask any question, your way, and collect the
insights you need to make smarter decisions.

### Reach Your Audience Anywhere

Share your survey in a snap. Distribute via email, social media, or embedded links to reach your
audience wherever they are. With a single click, your survey is optimized for mobile, tablet, and
desktop, ensuring a flawless experience on any device.

[Survey Distribution Options]
[Data Analysis Tools]

### Unlock Actionable Insights Instantly

Transform raw data into powerful insights with Super Survey's real-time reporting and visual
analytics. Our AI-driven sentiment analysis dives deeper into responses, helping you uncover
emotions, trends, and patterns in seconds. Whether you're identifying customer pain points or
workforce sentiments, our analytics give you the clarity to make smarter, faster decisions.

Easily export your results to Excel for detailed analysis or integrate seamlessly with your
workflow. Plus, stay updated with instant email notifications whenever new responses come in. With
Super Survey's built-in analytics and AI-powered tools, your data becomes your ultimate competitive
advantage - delivering insights as soon as they happen.

### Seamlessly Integrate Your Workflow

Connect your surveys to the tools you already use, like Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, and more.
Automate data management and simplify your workflow with integrations that keep everything in sync,
so you can focus on what matters most.

[Abstract image showing survey maker saving time during the results analysis part of survey]

### Less Time Building Surveys, More Time Learning from Your Audience

At Super Survey, we know what matters most: creating surveys that are free from bias, accurate, and
packed with insights. Our platform is designed to help you get surveys done quickly and effectively.
With our AI-driven tools, you can craft surveys that deliver lessons, not just data, ensuring your
results are both meaningful and actionable. Skip the guesswork - Super Survey is built to make your
surveys smarter, faster, and better every step of the way.

### Built-In Security You Can Trust

Your data's safety is our top priority. Super Survey utilizes industry-leading encryption to ensure
every survey and response remains secure. Hosted on US-based dedicated servers with robust security
compliance standards, we go above and beyond to protect your information. Whether you're collecting
sensitive business insights or personal data, you can trust Super Survey to provide a secure
environment. With our commitment to top-tier security, you can focus on gathering insights with
complete confidence.

[Secure Survey Platform]

## 10 Things You Need to Do to Make Your Survey Excel

## Keep it Short

Length is one of the strongest predictors of survey completion. A [study by Galesic and Bosnjak in
Public Opinion Quarterly][14] showed that every additional minute of survey length reduces
completion and degrades response quality, and an [analysis of 25,080 real web surveys by Revilla and
Ochoa][15] places the practical ceiling at around 10 minutes before drop-off accelerates. Our own
analysis of more than 1 million survey responses confirms it: surveys with 5 or fewer multiple
choice questions have a 24% higher completion rate than those with 6 to 8 questions. Every question
should serve a purpose, to help you take action, not just gather data. If your respondents see value
in every question, they'll stay engaged and complete the survey.

1
2

## Multiple Choice & Checkboxes

Closed-format questions consistently outperform open-ended ones, especially when used as the first
question. Research by [Couper, Tourangeau, Conrad and Zhang on the design of grids in web
surveys][16] shows that matrix or grid layouts produce significantly higher item nonresponse, longer
completion times, and more straightlining than the same questions presented individually. Lean on
multiple choice and checkbox formats to keep cognitive load low and momentum high. Avoid matrix
questions wherever possible, since they often feel overwhelming by combining multiple questions into
one. Make your survey inviting by simplifying your questions, and give participants a feeling of
progress as they answer.

## Show One Question at a Time

Pagination reduces perceived effort and keeps respondents engaged. Work by [Toepoel, Das and Van
Soest in Field Methods][17] manipulated the number of items per screen and found that item
nonresponse rises as more questions are crammed onto a single page, while respondent satisfaction
with the layout drops. Our own analysis of more than 1 million survey responses found that surveys
displaying one question per page had a 31% higher completion rate than those showing multiple
questions per page. Our survey creator uses this setting by default. Keep the interface simple,
intuitive, and focused on helping participants move through each question easily.

3
4

## Avoid Progress Bars

Progress indicators are a double-edged design choice. A [meta-analysis of 32 experiments by Villar,
Callegaro and Yang in Social Science Computer Review][18] found that progress bars produce small
effects at best, and slow-moving ones can actually increase break-off by reminding respondents how
much remains. In a [field experiment by Yan, Conrad, Tourangeau and Couper in the International
Journal of Public Opinion Research][19], progress feedback backfired on longer surveys where
respondents had expected a short task. Instead of a bar, rely on clear navigation and positive
reinforcement. Let people focus on the current question without worrying about how far they have
left to go.

## Personalize Invitations

Personalized invitations meaningfully lift response. A [field experiment by Heerwegh in Public
Opinion Quarterly][20] found that adding the recipient's name to the salutation raised response
rates by roughly 8 percentage points, and a large-scale experiment by [Sauermann and Roach in
Research Policy][21] found personalization increased the odds of responding by as much as 48%.
Whenever possible, let respondents know in advance that a survey is coming. Personal touches like
using their name or referencing specific topics they care about can make all the difference. Think
about how you would like to be addressed if you were in their shoes.

5
6

## Explain Why the Survey Matters

People are more likely to participate when they understand the purpose. When respondents feel that
their input will lead to meaningful changes, they are far more inclined to participate. As Professor
Robert Cialdini's classic work on influence demonstrated, providing a reason, even a simple one,
materially increases compliance with a request. Show your participants that their time matters, and
that their input is crucial in making informed decisions. State up front what the data will be used
for and what changes their answers may shape.

## ‍What does travel insurance cover?

Even the best-planned trips can take an unexpected turn. That’s where travel insurance coverage
comes in. It’s your protection for travel mishaps—from cancellations and flight delays to lost
baggage and medical emergencies far from home. So, what does travel insurance cover? It can
reimburse you for non-refundable expenses, cover emergency medical expenses, and even help with
things like missing connections or stolen passports. In short, it can help you travel with peace of
mind—knowing you’re covered, wherever the road (or sky) takes you.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What should I list as my destination?

You can enter one or multiple destinations when getting a quote. If you are visiting multiple
countries, you can enter each into the “Destinations” field. However, you are only required to enter
one.

It’s important to note that there are a few restricted destinations we do not provide travel
protection for. For this reason, we recommend entering all destinations.

### What does travel insurance from Travel Insured cover?

Travel insurance benefits can provide coverage for losses or expenses incurred while traveling, such
as cancellations, medical emergencies, and more

### Do I need travel insurance?

Some countries may require proof of travel insurance, in which case we hope you choose Travel
Insured International for your trip. For other scenarios where travel insurance is not mandatory, we
still recommend getting a plan especially for travelers who are traveling internationally and may
have significant non-refundable expenses, or want protection against unexpected events like medical
emergencies or trip cancellations. Ultimately, travel insurance can provide peace of mind and some
financial security—helping you to relax just a little bit more.

### How does travel insurance work?

Travel insurance helps protect against unexpected events that may occur before or during your trip,
such as trip cancellations, medical emergencies, or lost luggage. When you purchase a plan, you pay
a cost based on your trip details and coverage needs. If a covered event happens, you file a claim
with us, submit any required documentation, and, if approved, receive reimbursement for your
eligible expenses up to the plan’s maximum benefit amount.

### How much is travel insurance?

The cost of travel protection varies depending on factors such as your trip duration, age, and the
level of coverage you choose. Additional coverage options, such as our Flight Bundle or Cruise
Bundle, are an additional cost to the base plan. Comparing plans and coverage details can help you
find the best value for your specific travel needs.

*All plans contain insurance benefits and non-insurance travel assistance services.*

### Is travel insurance worth it?

Travel protection may be worth it for travelers, particularly when taking international trips or
making significant non-refundable bookings. It offers essential protection against unexpected events
such as medical emergencies, trip cancellations, or lost luggage, which can otherwise be pricey
without reimbursement. Overall, for anyone seeking peace of mind and some financial security while
traveling, purchasing travel protection can be a good choice.

## All types of plans for all types of people

### [Health insurance plans][13]

Explore a range of individual and family plan options, including ACA Marketplace plans.

### [Medicare plans][14]

Find coverage that goes beyond Original Medicare, including Medicare Advantage plans.

### [Medicaid plans][15]

See Medicaid plan options if you have low income or qualify due to a special circumstance.

### [Dental, vision and supplemental plans][16]

Browse plans that can help you get coverage for medical costs not covered by your medical plan.

## Frequently asked questions about health insurance

### What is health insurance?

Health insurance is a plan, or policy, that covers a percentage of doctors’ visits and hospital
bills. It helps offset the costs of both planned and unplanned medical needs. Medical care can be
expensive, but health insurance may help lessen the financial burden.

And health insurance isn’t just for when you’re sick or injured. It can also help you stay healthy
through preventive care and wellness programs. This may help you save money, too, by catching
potential health concerns before they become larger issues.

### How does health insurance work?

Health insurance is a contract between you and an insurance company (the insurer). When you purchase
a plan, you become a member of that plan. Each month, you’ll likely pay a fee, called a premium, to
use the plan.

There are many different types of health plans, but they generally work the same way. You pay for
some medical costs and your insurer pays for some costs. How those costs break out depend on your
specific plan benefits and coverage.

[Learn more about how health insurance works][17]

### How do I get health insurance?

Finding the right health insurance plan depends on a variety of factors. These include things like
your age, health and financial situation. For example, if you’re over 65 or have a qualifying
disability or special situation, you may be eligible for [Medicare][18]. If you have a lower income,
you may qualify for [Medicaid][19]. If you want to purchase an individual plan, an [Affordable Care
Act (ACA)][20] plan could be an option. Or, you may have the option to get [health insurance through
your employer][21].

Most health insurance plans have a special period of time, usually once a year, when you can enroll.
This is called open enrollment. It’s when you can start, stop or change your health plan. Timing of
open enrollment varies based on the plan.

[Learn more about open enrollment][22]

### What are the different types of health insurance?

There are a variety of health insurance plans that fit different needs. Some plans are offered
through the government, like [Affordable Care Act (ACA)][23] plans, [Medicare][24] plans and
[Medicaid][25] plans. There are also health plans you can get through your employer. Or, you can
purchase a plan on your own, like [short term health insurance][26] that offers coverage for a
limited amount of time. Understanding the different health insurance options can help you find the
plan that may work best for you.

You may also see terms like HMO, PPO, EPO and POS ­— these refer to the four basic kinds of provider
networks that certain health plans may offer. A network may include doctors, hospitals and other
providers that agree to provide services to plan members at a negotiated rate. This may help lower
your out-of-pocket costs.

[Learn more about the different types of health insurance][27]

### How much does health insurance cost?

It depends. A variety of factors impact how much you pay. These can include your age, your location
and lifestyle habits. It also depends on the type of plan you choose. With some plans, you may pay
less up front, but more when you receive care. For other plans, the opposite can be true.

[Learn more about health insurance costs][28]

a plan, you become a member of that plan. Each month, you’ll likely pay a fee, called a premium, to
use the plan.

There are many different types of health plans, but they generally work the same way. You pay for
some medical costs and your insurer pays for some costs. How those costs break out depend on your
specific plan benefits and coverage.

[Learn more about how health insurance works][17]

### How do I get health insurance?

Finding the right health insurance plan depends on a variety of factors. These include things like
your age, health and financial situation. For example, if you’re over 65 or have a qualifying
disability or special situation, you may be eligible for [Medicare][18]. If you have a lower income,
you may qualify for [Medicaid][19]. If you want to purchase an individual plan, an [Affordable Care
Act (ACA)][20] plan could be an option. Or, you may have the option to get [health insurance through
your employer][21].

Most health insurance plans have a special period of time, usually once a year, when you can enroll.
This is called open enrollment. It’s when you can start, stop or change your health plan. Timing of
open enrollment varies based on the plan.

[Learn more about open enrollment][22]

### What are the different types of health insurance?

There are a variety of health insurance plans that fit different needs. Some plans are offered
through the government, like [Affordable Care Act (ACA)][23] plans, [Medicare][24] plans and
[Medicaid][25] plans. There are also health plans you can get through your employer. Or, you can
purchase a plan on your own, like [short term health insurance][26] that offers coverage for a
limited amount of time. Understanding the different health insurance options can help you find the
plan that may work best for you.

You may also see terms like HMO, PPO, EPO and POS ­— these refer to the four basic kinds of provider
networks that certain health plans may offer. A network may include doctors, hospitals and other
providers that agree to provide services to plan members at a negotiated rate. This may help lower
your out-of-pocket costs.

[Learn more about the different types of health insurance][27]

### How much does health insurance cost?

It depends. A variety of factors impact how much you pay. These can include your age, your location
and lifestyle habits. It also depends on the type of plan you choose. With some plans, you may pay
less up front, but more when you receive care. For other plans, the opposite can be true.

[Learn more about health insurance costs][28]

### What does health insurance cover?

Coverage is unique to each health plan. Many plans may cover things like preventive care,
prescription drugs, hospital stays, mental health services and more. A plan may cover the full cost
of certain services, or you may have to share costs (by paying a copay or coinsurance, for example)
until you meet a deductible or out-of-pocket limit.

Make sure to review benefits and coverage before choosing a plan. You can find this information in
the plan’s Summary of Benefits and Coverage. This is a document that all health plan companies are
required to provide. It outlines what’s covered, partially covered or not covered under a health
plan.

[Learn how to review a Summary of Benefits and Coverage][29]
[Learn more about health insurance][30]
[Get the facts about how the health system works][31]

## Working to make the health care experience better

UnitedHealthcare puts care at the heart of health insurance. Empathy, transparency and human
connection guide us. Because better care comes from understanding what people need — and making
quality care more personal.
